_about: The one place for the core rules' version and change history. tools/build-website.py reads it for the core-rules page and the changelog. rulesVersion and rulesUpdated change only when the rules (mechanics) change; a website or wording update adds a 'site' entry and leaves them alone. rulesVersion is null until the author picks a numbering scheme.

changes.title: Aurora: Toughness boxes, and harm above Class IV
items: A hero gets one Toughness box for each Class of their best Defense (Toughness, a Force Field, an Aegis suit). Toughness boxes are marked before the three Injury boxes, carry no penalty, and clear when the fight ends.
Against anyone with more than 3 boxes, Class V attacks mark 4 boxes and Class VI mark 5, before Defense.
An Aegis suit now gives its Toughness II (physical and energy) in the GM view's encounters, as the guide says.
The sheet, the GM cards, the battle map tokens and the shared table show the Toughness boxes; ending an encounter clears them.

changes.title: Aurora: a telling hit gets through any Defense
items: An attack at or below a Defense's Class still marks 1 box on a telling hit (made by 5 or more, or a natural 3 or 4). Attacks a Class above it still mark a box fewer, and a telling one always marks at least 1.
This is Aurora's one exception to the core rule that a telling hit never adds boxes.
In test fights the party went from never beating a Defense IV-VI villain to winning 93% against Steel Hawk, about 80% against Helios and Grachyov, and 43-44% against Autuarch and the Atomic Man.

changes.title: Alternate forms with their own numbers
items: Any character can have their own alternate form (Powers step): its name and their normal shape's, attribute, Dodge and Move changes, the powers that work only in the form, and a note.

The sheet's and the table card's form switch, skills, Dodge, Move and the Encounter panel all use the form's numbers while the character is in it; a form-only power gives no attack, Defense or move outside it.

changes.title: Aurora: every notable Operant as a ready-made sheet
items: Eight supers the history names now have stat blocks: Herbert Unler, Zarloff the Elder, the Ivory Phoenix, Charlie Swift, Warlord I, Armageddon, Johnny Vanroy (Mr. Power) and John Marcus Mars Jr.
All 30 named Operants are ready-made sheets for the GM, built from their stat blocks; the GM view adds them as NPCs. Mr. Marvel, Uathach and the Ice Reaper come with their alternate forms.

changes.title: Aurora: Piercing, and the neurogun
items: Piercing (armor-piercing rounds): a piercing attack meets a Defense one Class higher than it is, but marks its own Class's boxes. Armor with a Defense rating protects as usual; a plain body armor vest doesn't help against it.

The flechette rifle is Class II, Piercing. The neurogun is an advanced taser: a Class II physical stun, Body −4 to stay up, which Defense II stops. A stun weapon with a Class now meets Defense like any other attack.

changes.title: Aurora: damage types and the Vulnerability complication
items: Four damage types: physical, energy, mystic and mind. Each Defense covers its own (Toughness physical; Force Field physical and energy); against another type it counts one Class lower. No Defense but Mind Defense helps against the mind, and force made by the mind is physical.
Weak (a box more), resistant (Defense +1) and immune (nothing below Class VI) to a type, element or material. The Vulnerability complication is a weakness chosen with the GM.

changes.title: Aurora: Defense takes an attack one Class above it
items: An attack must be at least one Class above a Defense to do anything, and then marks one box fewer; an equal or lower one does nothing (before, an equal attack marked a box fewer and a higher one hit in full). Falls follow: Toughness II walks away from a rooftop, IV from a tower, V from a fall from a plane.

changes.title: Aurora: unstable powers come in levels
items: Unstable I flares on a natural 18 with Powers, II on 17–18, III on 16–18, IV on 15–18. Lab-made gives Unstable II; the Unstable Powers complication gives the level chosen (I to III); the two add, to IV. The GM can raise or lower a level in play, and Strain 3 flares any power on 16–18.

changes.title: Aurora: the Foundation's retrieval teams, and Dead Air
items: Retrieval teams carry neuroguns, flechette rifles and stun grenades besides their tranquilizers and dampening net, and will kill to leave no witnesses (a Foundation hardware table in the GM's Guide).
The first case is now Dead Air, and Subject 19 has no codename.

changes.title: No one starts below 10
items: Origins only raise attributes, and their bonuses come out of the five attribute points, so every origin starts with the same total. Custom and homebrew origins: 0 to +2 each, +3 at most.
Ordinary people: 10 in every attribute, Dodge 8, Move 5 yards, 6 in anything untrained. An attribute drops below 10 only for a reason in play: an injury, a curse, a form.
The pregenerated characters are rebalanced to match, and older characters are put right when they're opened.

changes.title: The GM view: NPCs, powers on the cards, and the playtests in one click
items: NPCs (the people the characters meet) are full characters in the GM view, from any threat or written in: their own boxes, portrait and token, linked to their battle map token, and on their own side in the Encounter panel.
Table cards list powers by Class and spells, show a power's move apart from the move on foot, and label the injury boxes; the same character isn't added twice unless they're a generic NPC.
A playtest loads in one click: its campaign, the ready-made characters, its NPCs, clocks and files, and each scene's map with its enemies (who grow with the adventure's threat).

changes.title: Music, battle maps and character pictures
items: Music for each setting, to play at the table or download; battle maps, tokens and portraits for the playtests, from the table server, with replaced pictures picked up.

changes.title: The settings and the core rules, brought in line
items: What the settings had worked out separately is now in the core rules, for every setting: chases where one side is clearly faster, chases by range (an opposed roll moves the range a band), and a damage track for vehicles; acting first and acting more than once a round; helping in a fight; pins that hold against someone much stronger.
Falls mark boxes by height (a story 1, a rooftop 2, a tower 3 and Dying, higher is certain death), with fire and foul air beside them. Every setting's fall uses it; Aurora's adds Classes.

Conditions, defined once: stunned, Frightened (keep away from the source, −2 against it, Will each turn to shake it) and Charmed. The settings' fear spells and horrors (Grave Chill, Dread, the Thing from the Deep, Emotion Control) now say Frightened.

Weapons: what "3, and Dying" means, explosions, stun weapons and jams; and armor, toughness, weaknesses and materials, the way every setting's gear and threats already use them. Guns now jam on a natural 18 in Trails of Blood & Dust too, as in the other settings.

Investigation: a head start (a character trained in the right field skips Confront) and a rival clock, from Fracture Lines; and enemies' files on the characters (+2 when it applies, destroyed when found), from Aurora, now in every setting's GM view.

Tracks: shared and personal tracks described once. A Mind track (Aurora's mental harm) is described as an option any setting can use; its middle box is now Overwhelmed, since Reeling is the Shattered Crown's word for stunned.
Smaller fixes: The Shattered Crown's Charm is resisted with Will (it said Presence), as everywhere else; Fracture Lines' ship fights are described as they're actually run.

changes.title: Aurora: mind powers, a Mind track and Mind Defense
items: Every character has a Mind track of three boxes beside the injury track: Shaken (−1 to mental actions), Overwhelmed (−2), Broken (unconscious or catatonic). Psychic attacks mark it; it never leaves anyone Dying, and a night's sleep clears it. It's on the play tab, the printed sheet, the GM view's cards and the battle map.

Mind Defense from Telepathy, Mind Control, Possession or an ExLAW psi-dampening headset: a weaker mind power does nothing, an equal one is resisted at +2. A Class IV mind against someone without it is resisted at −2.
Psychic attacks: Telepathy II (a psychic stab) and Illusion III (fears made real), one Class below the power, Powers against Will, never Dodge, Toughness or Force Field.

Rules for reading minds (and being noticed), mind links, being controlled (the player keeps playing; +2 against a harmful command, +4 against hurting a friend; Spark for another roll), emotions, illusions and sensing lies.

The Encounter panel resolves psychic attacks as Will contests on the Mind track (Lord Marrow's nightmare no longer meets Toughness or Dodge), and the sheet's roller applies the Mind penalty to mental actions.

changes.title: Aurora: speed, flight, height and falling
items: Speed, Flight and Super Leaping move a range band in a fight: Medium at Class I, Long at II, Extreme at III, anywhere in the scene from IV. The sheet's Move shows it.

Speed's steps, evened out: acts first (I), a second defense and blows at speed (II), two actions once a scene (III), two actions a round (IV), three (V). Blows at speed hit one Class below your Speed. Celerity's now hit at Class III.
Chases against vehicles: a car is Class I, a helicopter II, a jet III, a fighter IV; a higher Class wins without a roll.

Height counts in the distance (and on the battle map, where a token can have a height). Dives hit one Class higher; carrying slows you a Class; a flier stunned, knocked out or knocked back falls unless they make a Powers roll.
A fall is an attack with a Class by its height (I to IV), so Toughness protects against it.
The Encounter panel puts Speed first in the turn order, gives the extra actions and the second defense, offers a Dive to fliers, and warns when a flier falls.

changes.title: Aurora: super strength, and every power's attacks in the Encounter panel
items: Super strength has its own rules: lifting (one step past your Class is a push), objects with a Class to break, throwing (Athletics; a car also hits everyone next to the target), weapons in strong hands (the higher Class; ordinary weapons break above Class II), knockback from Class III, and pins that hold against weaker targets (Body −2 per Class of difference).
Strength and Size give +2 to Body for feats and breaking holds: a new choice in the sheet's roller.

A player character's attack powers now come into the Encounter panel at their Class: Strength (blows and throws), Natural Weapons, Blast, Telekinesis, Elemental and Weather Control, Gravity, Shadow, Manifest and Stretching. Before, a hero with powers fought there with fists and gear only.
The Encounter panel applies strong hands and logs knockback and how hard a pin is to break.

changes.title: Aurora: Exposure, villains' files and team-ups
items: A character with a Secret Identity has Exposure, a track of four boxes: marked when the secret slips, cleared by alibis. When it fills, the hero is unmasked and the player chooses the price. It shows on the play tab and in the GM view.

Exposure is relative: each hero keeps a list of who already knows the secret (family, a team, ExLAW, a villain). A legal status adds its own (Registered: the EMD; Reserve Agent: ExLAW's Director). Exposure measures the secret getting past them, and someone new who learns it goes on the list.
Villains keep files on the heroes: what they know, and +2 against that hero when it applies. The GM records them in the GM view; a hero who finds a file sees it on their sheet, and can destroy it.
Team-ups: two heroes combine powers in one action. The attack counts one Class higher and both mark a box of Strain. The Encounter panel has a Team-up choice for attacks with a Class.

changes.title: Aurora: stats for every named character
items: Every Notable Operant in Aurora's GM's Guide now has a stat block: Class, attacks, Dodge, boxes, Defense, powers, skills and what makes them who they are at the table. Autuarch, master of the White Hand, gets an entry of his own.

All 22 are in the GM view, in the Encounter panel and on the battle map, under their name and Class. Their Defense works as the rules say: an attack below it does nothing, one equal to it marks a box fewer.

changes.title: The campaign builder, with card triggers
items: The GM view has a Campaign tab: the campaign's premise and themes, an outline of adventures, people, places, factions, and sessions (the plan, the log and a recap for the players). Save it to a file, or open one.
Roll any of them from the setting's own tables: adventure seeds, key characters, places, threats, allegiances and names. A rolled entry opens in its form, to change before you keep it.
Triggers: a step of the outline can stay locked until the group holds the cards it names, and as many as you ask for. Then it unlocks for good and tells the GM what happens.

Share any entry with the players: they see its public part on their play tab, through the shared table; never a secret or the GM's notes. A shared locked step shows as locked, and what opens it if the GM says so.

changes.title: The GM view and GM's Guides open to everyone; homebrew origins and advantages
items: Every creator's GM view and GM's Guide are open again, and the GM's Guides are back on the setting pages in Word. A GM access code is needed only to start a shared table on this site: ask for one in the Discord server or by email.

Homebrew now takes origins (tier, attribute changes, origin skills, origin advantages and their complications; in Aurora, powers like one of the setting's origins) and advantages (+2 to a narrow task with a skill). They join the creator's choices like the setting's own.
Want your own table server on Cloudflare? Ask, and we'll send you the package.

changes.title: A dev blog and the community Discord
items: The new Dev blog page carries news from the making of the game: rules changes, the settings, playtest notes and what's coming. Filter it by setting, or read every post.
The home page shows the latest three posts.
Join the Legend Dynamics Discord server from the home page, the Discord page or any page's footer, or at legenddynamicsrpg.com/join.

changes.title: Homebrew: your own threats, weapons, Edges, cards, powers, spells and rituals
items: The GM view has a Homebrew tab: make your own threats, weapons and Edges with simple forms, no code. They work like the setting's own, marked homebrew, in the Encounter panel, on the battle map, in characters' gear and the roller, and in the creator's Edges.

Cards, spells and rituals too: homebrew lore cards, data records, dossiers and tales join the subjects the GM records findings with (and Trails' Hunter's Almanac); homebrew hexes, cantrips and psionic powers, and Aurora's powers (what each does at Class I to VI), join the creator's choices; homebrew rituals make a ritual book beside Rituals by heart.
Players get the GM's homebrew when they join the shared table, or from a homebrew file.

Bonuses the table works out, chosen from menus: a weapon's accuracy, strong hits and what it's made of; a threat's hard hide, weaknesses, what alone can hurt it, how hard it is to hit and a second defense; an Edge's skill, Dodge or Move bonus, a second defense or shrugging off a telling hit; an attack spell, cast in the Encounter panel. The sheet, the roller, the shared table and the Encounter panel use them.
The core rules' Making your own chapter gives the numbers to keep homebrew in line with the book's.

changes.title: Fracture Lines: example data records, the Countdown and skill
items: Seven example data records in the GM's Guide: a Halvane lattice core, the Warden of the Ashkarr, a corridor engine, a spatial fracture, a living hull, corporate black-site encryption and an alien weapon cache, each with what goes wrong in each phase.
The Countdown no longer runs on routine discovery: the GM starts one after a failed roll or a success at a cost, when the stakes are real.
A character trained in the skill that fits the subject can skip Confront the unknown.
Rival clocks: an ordinary danger clock for whoever is racing the crew to the same find.

changes.title: Trails of Blood & Dust: special loads and the hunter's shot
items: Special loads: silver rounds, rock salt shells, cold iron shot, blessed rounds and incendiary shells, tracked as three uses a job each rather than counted bullets. Silver bullets in the gear list become silver rounds.
A load works against the weakness it's made of, whoever fires it. With a lore card for the creature and the matching load, a hunter's shot makes the called shot or effect the card permits.
Coming by loads can cost: buying silver marks Whispers only if folks learn what it's for, and church silver or the makings of fire mark Heat. Blessed rounds burn a demon but never banish it.
A wraith can now be hurt by rock salt in the Encounter panel, as its weakness already said.

changes.title: Legend cards and the price of information
items: A Legend card records one thing the characters have established: the finding, its limits, the evidence or source, how it was learned, what it cost, and who holds it. Each setting names its cards.
A card can be earned by a discovery clock, or directly: seen or tested firsthand, a reliable account, or the subject's own word backed by evidence.
Information is never free: each direct source has a price, ticking the threat clock or a track. A clock's card costs what the clock already cost. Proposing an idea is free.
A real weakness works whether or not anyone holds a card for it.
A new section for the GM: making Legend cards.

changes.title: Fracture Lines, Aurora and The Shattered Crown: data records, dossiers and tales
items: Fracture Lines keeps data records in an archive, Aurora dossiers in a binder, and The Shattered Crown tales in a saga, each with its own chapter in both guides.
The Shattered Crown gains discovery clocks, racing its Doom track.
New advantages give three starting cards the player writes: secrets from their role or origin that aren't common knowledge.
Trails of Blood & Dust: each source of a lore card now has its price.

changes.title: Trails of Blood & Dust: renewing a talisman
items: A broken talisman (the Talisman Edge) is renewed only between jobs, and only by going back to its maker or another worker of the same tradition. Until then it stays spent.

changes.title: Website and editorial improvements
items: A Start here page: choose a setting, create a character, join or run a game.
Shorter Play online section on the home page, linking to the shared-table and Discord pages for setup.
The four settings now call a character's role a role everywhere (the home page and creators said calling). Same choices, same saved characters.
Small wording fixes in the core rules (an origin, a role), and one copyright notice per page.
This changelog, and the rules' last-updated date on the core-rules page.

changes.title: Movement, reach and range bands
items: Tighter range bands: Short 25 yards, Medium 100, Long 300, Extreme 1,000; Close stays 10. Running covers 20 yards.
Move: each character has a Move in yards, worked out from their attributes, Athletics and origin; Run is twice Move.
Weapon reach: every weapon in hand has a reach of 1, 2 or 3 yards.
Injury and hard going slow Move; stepping away from a fight is free.
Telling-hit effects depend on the weapon: Pin needs a weapon in hand, fists or a grapple.
Origin speed adjustments, and mounts and vehicles.

changes.title: Balance revision
items: Fine weapons and tools: +2 to one narrowly defined use of a skill, never a defense.
Additional Defense: a second defense each round at −2.
Magic limits: Quicker hand, every hostile burst names a defense or a resistance, personal magic marks at most 3 boxes, and charms still face the target's defense.
Telling hits: Break gear, Pin, Precise and Knock down clarified, with firm limits.
Medical treatment: one field-treatment and one proper-care attempt per set of injuries.
